scenarios.boundary: provider policy admission and request N+1
scenarios.observed: two requests admitted at limit 2; request 3 refused pretransport with receipt

scenarios.boundary: external proposer request N/N+1 at HTTP boundary
scenarios.expected: request N is admitted; request N+1 is refused before fixture/upstream forwarding and retained in the campaign receipt
scenarios.observed: real OpenCode CLI emitted multiple provider HTTP requests; exactly one request was fixture-forwarded, N+1 received 429, and the sanitized receipt was persisted without retry

scenarios.boundary: candidate patch scope and resume identity
scenarios.observed: scope and stale identity refusals asserted

scenarios.boundary: candidate build correction and retry limit
scenarios.expected: correct only within the declared retry ceiling
scenarios.observed: bounded retry counts and build rerun asserted

scenarios.boundary: independent verifier and candidate score integrity
scenarios.expected: reject incomplete, relabeled, or control-regressing results
scenarios.observed: negative controls, partial pairings, independent fixture outcomes, and score decisions covered

scenarios.result: pass; synthetic proposer/qualification boundary, production score contract and optimizer/checkpoint/worktree code

scenarios.boundary: SIGKILL across checkpoint and ledger append boundaries
scenarios.expected: record interrupted_unknown and do not duplicate a scored pair
scenarios.observed: crash recovery state and exactly-once row assertions pass

scenarios.boundary: timeout, cleanup, cancellation, disk state and private subject isolation
scenarios.expected: bounded terminal and cleanup; no cross-subject teardown
scenarios.observed: local subprocess tests pass; exact-main smoke stopped subject 1 while subject 2 completed session creation

scenarios.boundary: controller SIGKILL and private subject daemon reconciliation
scenarios.expected: after parent death, the exact private daemon is gone or stopped by verified lane identity; default daemon and unrelated sentinel survive
scenarios.observed: controller was SIGKILLed after a real ACP session; the private daemon was absent or safely stopped through exact lane identity; sentinel remained live and default daemon identity was unchanged

scenarios.boundary: parallel Cargo CPU/target contention and repeat recovery
scenarios.expected: two parallel offline Cargo checks with one worker each use disjoint private target roots; the real optimizer admits and records its candidate while both checks remain active; the sequence repeats without leakage
scenarios.observed: both Cargo checks were observed active at each optimizer proposal boundary in two bounded rounds; both checks then passed and temporary targets were removed

scenarios.boundary: campaign transition and side-effect fault mapping
scenarios.expected: proposal admission, patch capture, build, independent verifier, ACP evaluation, score publication, checkpoint pointer, ledger append, cancellation, private-daemon cleanup and resource-floor failures each map to a named injected refusal/recovery with no duplicate admission or scored row
scenarios.observed: SIGKILL was injected at six persisted optimizer phases and recovered from durable phase state without a second proposal; exception injection covered the same six phases; checkpoint-pointer and ledger-append SIGKILLs retained exactly-once assertions; parent-death cleanup preserved the default daemon and unrelated sentinel

limits: No real external proposer HTTP request was made; the live route remains unavailable until a separate authorization and exact endpoint check.

The candidate controller sequence uses a synthetic proposer and qualification boundary; native CodeGG ACP/job qualification is exercised separately and is not claimed as an optimizer-integrated paired campaign.
Cargo contention is bounded to two capped checks in two rounds; it proves optimizer progress during active work but is not a prolonged saturation campaign.
SIGKILL phase recovery uses durable phase boundaries and an injected qualification callback; it does not kill the controller inside every Rust build or native ACP subprocess instruction window.
No provider-backed campaign or stable-live claim is implied.
